subtopics.title: Force Without Touching — the Idea of a Field

questions.question: A magnetic field is defined as:
options: A stream of particles flowing from north to south
A region in space where another magnet or ferromagnetic material experiences a force
The metal core inside a magnet
An electric current in a wire

questions.question: Match the field to what it acts on: gravitational, electric, magnetic act respectively on:
options: Mass; charge; magnets and ferromagnetic materials

questions.question: Which group of materials is ferromagnetic?
A key difference between the gravitational field and the other two fields is that gravity:

subtopics.title: Poles Come in Pairs — and the Pair Cannot Be Divorced

questions.question: Two north poles brought close together will:
A bar magnet is cut in half. Each half:
options: Is a pure north or a pure south pole
Is a complete magnet with both a north and a south pole

questions.question: A magnetic monopole — an isolated north or south pole — is:
options: The end of any compass needle

questions.question: In a ferromagnetic material, domains are:
options: Regions where the tiny magnetic fields of electrons line up
The two ends of the magnet

subtopics.title: Drawing the Invisible — Magnetic Field Lines

questions.question: Outside a magnet, field lines run:
options: In closed circles around the middle
From the north pole to the south pole

questions.question: Closely spaced field lines at a point indicate:
Field lines never cross because a crossing would mean:
options: The field points in two directions at one point, which is meaningless

questions.question: Iron filings around a bar magnet show the field's shape but not its:
options: Direction — small compasses are needed for that

questions.question: A compass needle points north because:
options: The needle is heavier at one end
It is a small magnet aligning with the Earth's magnetic field
The geographic pole pulls all metals

questions.question: Since the north pole of a needle points toward the Arctic, the Earth's magnetic pole there behaves like:
The geographic North Pole is:
options: The northernmost point of the Earth's axis of rotation
The exact spot every compass points to
A wandering point in the core
The strongest part of the Earth's field

questions.question: Auroras near the poles occur when:
options: Moonlight reflects off the ice caps
The core's iron glows through the crust
Solar-wind particles are funnelled along field lines into the upper atmosphere

questions.question: The fridge magnet is snatched to the door before touching it because:
options: The door's field reaches out to all metals
The door is inside the magnet's field, and steel feels the force

questions.question: The magnet's bubble of influence is strongest:
options: Right at the magnet, fading fast with distance

questions.question: A magnet holds a paper note against a steel fridge door because:
options: The paper is invisible to the field — the magnet grips the steel through it

questions.question: Snipping a magnetised pin in half to keep only the north end produces:
options: A pure north half and a pure south half
One strong and one weak pole
Two complete magnets, each with a new pole at the cut

questions.question: In the crowd-doing-the-wave picture, a magnetised pin is one where:
options: The domains all face the same way
The domains point in random directions
North atoms sit at one end

questions.question: Dropping a magnet can weaken it because the jolt:
Stroking a steel needle repeatedly with a magnet, always in the same direction:
options: Heats the needle until it bends

questions.question: The magnetic north pole and the geographic North Pole are:
options: On opposite sides of the planet
Hundreds of kilometres apart, and the magnetic one drifts

questions.question: The Earth's magnetic field protects life by:
options: Deflecting most of the solar wind around the planet
Holding the atmosphere down with magnetic force

questions.question: A magnetic storm — the field shuddering after a violent solar eruption — can disrupt:
The Earth's magnetic field is thought to arise from:
options: A solid bar magnet buried at the core
The churning of molten iron in the core
